Samantha 3 thanks for the clear ask. I pulled together a lightweight approach below and attached a first-pass pricing deck (RW-pricing-draft_v1.xlsx). High-level proposal:

1) Cross-quarter flex-commit addendum
   - 3-month optional conversion: LedgerWise can convert up to 50% of the short-term flex volume into a committed tranche with a retroactive effective date (reduces unit cost).

2) Price-hold
   - Hold current published price for 6 months after renewal on committed units. If conversion to committed tranche happens, the hold applies to that committed baseline.

3) Burst credit pool
   - Provide an allocated burst pool equal to 20% of committed monthly tokens for a 3-month period; unused credits do not roll forward. Overages beyond the pool billed at pay-as-you-go.

4) Quick approval path
   - If procurement signs a short addendum, we can lock terms and present a DocuSign URL for execution.

Samantha 3 good notes. Per internal review (legal + finance + CS), here9s a concrete concession set we can propose as an addendum. I9m attaching a one-page PDF (proposal_addendum_ledgerwise.pdf) you can share with procurement. Key points: 

- Committed discount band:
  * 12-month commit: 12% off published unit price on committed units
  * 24-month commit: 18% off published unit price on committed units

- Cross-quarter flex conversion:
  * Up to 50% of short-term flex volume convertible to committed tranche within 90 days of renewal effective date. Conversion applies retroactively to start of renewal month.

- Price-hold terms:
  * Price-hold for 6 months from renewal on both published and first post-conversion invoice for converted tranches. No retroactive increases.

- Burst credit pool:
  * Initial burst pool = 25% of committed monthly tokens for three months. Unused burst credits expire and are not refundable; however, any excess true-up below committed baseline will be credited at 50% of published rate back to a one-time credit for the following billing cycle.

- Operational guardrails:
  * Monthly true-up window; transparent consumption reporting token-level in the Redwood Console; threshold alerts at 70%/90% usage.
